lesson.subject: science
lesson.title: Mini-beasts and Micro-habitats
lesson.summary: Small animals, the tiny places where they live, how to look for them kindly, and how to protect their homes.
learning_objectives: Name some mini-beasts and say where they live
Say how to look after mini-beasts and their homes

standards.text: Identify that most living things live in habitats to which they are suited; identify and name a variety of plants and animals in their habitats, including micro-habitats

success_criteria: I can name a mini-beast and its home
I can say what a micro-habitat is
I can say how to protect small animals
lesson.real_life: Ants and beetles after rain in a Pakistani field, and slugs, ladybirds and bees in a UK garden.

warm_up.prompt: How many legs does an ant have?
A snail lives in a shell.

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: where do tiny animals live?
blocks.say: Today we look for tiny animals. Where do they live?

blocks.alt: A garden snail with a stripy shell on a green leaf covered in raindrops
blocks.caption: A snail loves wet weather. Its shell protects its soft body.
blocks.credit: Photo by Olivier Piau on Unsplash
blocks.say: This snail is out after the rain. Its shell is its own little house.

blocks.markdown: **Mini-beasts** are small animals without a backbone.
blocks.say: Small animals are called mini-beasts. Snails, worms, ants and spiders are all mini-beasts.

scenes.caption: A snail.
scenes.say: A snail has no legs. It glides on one soft foot.

scenes.caption: An ant.
scenes.say: An ant has six legs. It carries food to its nest.

scenes.caption: A spider.
scenes.say: A spider has eight legs. A spider is not an insect.

question.prompt: Which one of these is a mini-beast?
question.hint: It is small and has a shell.
question.explanation: A snail is a very small animal, so it is a mini-beast.

blocks.markdown: A **micro-habitat** is a very small place where animals live.
blocks.say: A habitat is the place where an animal lives. A tiny habitat is called a micro-habitat.

scenes.caption: Under a log.
scenes.say: Under a log it is dark and damp. Woodlice like it there.

scenes.caption: In soil.
scenes.say: Soil is the home of the earthworm. It tunnels underground.

scenes.caption: On a flower.
scenes.say: A flower is a home too. Bees visit it for sweet nectar.

question.prompt: A micro-habitat can be as small as one stone.
question.hint: Think about what lives under a stone.
question.explanation: Small animals shelter under one stone, so it is a micro-habitat.

blocks.title: Sana the snail
blocks.transcript: I am Sana the snail. I am small, but my garden is big. My shell is my house. It keeps my soft body safe. I love rainy days. The wet leaves are my favourite. Wazir the worm lives in damp soil. He has no legs either. Wafa the woodlouse hides under a log. It is dark and damp there. Bees visit the flowers. They drink sweet nectar. Oh no! A big child lifts the log. We stay very still. The child puts the log back. Our home is safe. Goodnight!
blocks.caption: A snail tells where she and her friends live.

points: A micro-habitat is a tiny home
Logs, soil and flowers are micro-habitats
blocks.say: Let us remember. Mini-beasts are small animals. They live in tiny habitats.

terms.meaning: Small animals without a backbone, such as snails and ants.
A very small place where animals live.
The place where an animal or plant lives.
The sweet juice inside a flower.
A small grey animal with many legs that lives in damp places.

blocks.markdown: A **bug hunt** means looking for mini-beasts and putting them back.
blocks.say: Let us go on a bug hunt. We look gently and we never hurt anything.

scenes.caption: Lift slowly.
scenes.say: Lift a log slowly. Small animals may be hiding underneath.

scenes.caption: Look closely.
scenes.say: Use a magnifying glass. It helps us see tiny legs.

scenes.caption: Put it back.
scenes.say: Put the log back as you found it. That keeps their home safe.

question.prompt: Put the bug hunt steps in order.
question.explanation: We lift the log, look and count, then put the log back.

blocks.credit: Photo by An Shved on Unsplash
blocks.say: This red and black bug is walking on moss. Moss is a damp, soft micro-habitat.

blocks.say: Every mini-beast has a home that suits it. Some need damp, some need warmth.

scenes.caption: Worm.
scenes.say: An earthworm needs damp soil. Dry soil would hurt its skin.

scenes.caption: Woodlouse.
scenes.say: A woodlouse hides in a dark place. The damp keeps its body safe.

scenes.caption: Spider.
scenes.say: A spider spins its web in a corner. Flies get caught in it.

blocks.say: Let us remember. Each mini-beast needs its own kind of home.

terms.meaning: A place with the food, shelter and damp or warmth an animal needs.
A sticky net of thread made by a spider.
A long hole under the ground.

mini_quiz.prompt: What does a spider make to catch flies?
mini_quiz.explanation: A spider spins a web to catch flies.

blocks.markdown: We can **protect** mini-beasts by leaving their homes alone.
blocks.say: Small animals lose their homes when we tidy too much. A tidy garden can be empty.
Mini-beasts do big jobs. Worms mix soil and bees carry pollen.

blocks.markdown: Many animals need mini-beasts to eat.
blocks.say: Birds and hedgehogs eat mini-beasts. So they are part of a food chain.

scenes.caption: Log pile.
scenes.say: Leave a pile of logs in a quiet corner. Beetles will move in.

scenes.caption: Flowers.
scenes.say: Plant flowers for the bees. They will visit all summer.

scenes.caption: No poison.
scenes.say: Do not use poison. It harms every small animal, not only pests.

question.prompt: Pick two ways to help mini-beasts.
question.hint: Think about giving them homes and food.
question.explanation: Logs give shelter and flowers give food.

blocks.alt: A tall bug hotel built from wooden pallets, filled with logs, drilled wood and pine cones
blocks.caption: A bug hotel gives small animals a dry and safe place to stay.
blocks.credit: Photo by Mika Baumeister on Unsplash
blocks.say: A bug hotel is a pile of logs, bark and pine cones. Small animals shelter in the holes.

blocks.markdown: Mini-beasts live in gardens and fields all over the world.
blocks.say: In Pakistan, gardens and fields are full of ants and beetles after the rain.

blocks.markdown: Look after small animals wherever you live.
blocks.say: In the UK, hedges and gardens hide slugs, ladybirds and bees.

blocks.markdown: Be kind to every living thing.
blocks.say: Muslims are taught to be kind to all living things. Small ones too.

terms.meaning: To keep something safe from harm.
